description: Verify that DUT accepts a UDP datagram with maximum supported payload length (65 507 bytes — IPv4 max payload 65 535 minus 20 IP header minus 8 UDP header)
approach:
[Objective]
The largest legal IPv4 datagram is 65 535 octets (16-bit Total Length). Subtracting the 20-byte IP header and 8-byte UDP header leaves 65 507 bytes for UDP payload. DUT must accept this maximum size — typically delivered through IP fragmentation and reassembly.

[Scenario — chronological]
1. Tester → DUT: UDP datagram with payload = 65 507 bytes
   • Built via emitFragmentedUdpStimulus (the harness fragments and reassembles transparently)
   • Payload byte at index i = i & 0xFF — deterministic per-index pattern so the SCXML can pivot on length while pcap remains readable

2. Observation:
   • DUT's upper-tester reports receipt with payload length == 65 507 (the SCXML pivots on length, not byte content)

[Pass condition]
UT-query confirms DUT delivered a UDP with payload length 65 507.

[Fail condition]
• Fail_field_mismatch — DUT delivered with the wrong payload length
• Fail_timeout — UT-query never arrived (test infra issue)

verdicts.Fail_field_mismatch: DUT received UDP with unexpected payload length
verdicts.Fail_timeout: No UT confirmation for max-length UDP
